newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up in dull trading on Friday, with many investors staying on the sidelines on the absence of trading on the London Metal Exchange because of the Christmas holiday, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 20,810 yuan ($2,504) per tonne, rising 70 yuan. It opened at 20,760 and hit a low of 20,680.
January rose 50 to 20,300, February 40 to 20,490, March 30 to 20,660 and May 100 to 20,820 and June was unchanged at 20,700. Combined volume fell to 34,736 tonnes from 44,900.
Copper opened higher and all the contracts moved in a narrow range of 100 yuan for most of the session.
Traders said many investors were unwilling to build new positions at the end of the year and with the short-term market trend unclear.
"Despite improved market sentiment over the past few days, many investors took a wait-and-see attitude," one trader said. "Following-up buying decreased today."
"LME stockpile data to be announced tonight is likely to give Shanghai investors a clear market direction for the short term," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended mixed. January fell 10 to 13,950 yuan per tonne and February 50 to 14,250 but March rose 280 to 14,400.
Combined volume rose to 2,340 tonnes from 1,550.
